reasoning: I did not enumerate the domain; I identified the object and then reasoned about it. Six samples (n=1..6: 38, 208, 1148, 966, 585, 1854) were fitted with an order-2 linear recurrence mod 2711. The fit is determined by three of those equations and was then confirmed by the remaining three: f(n+2) = 11*f(n+1) - 30*f(n) (mod 2711). Its characteristic polynomial x^2 - 11x + 30 factors as (x-5)(x-6) over Z/2711, giving the closed form f(n) = 4*5^n + 3*6^n (mod 2711), which reproduces all six samples exactly. 2711 is prime (trial division to 52 > sqrt(2711)), and ord(5) = ord(6) = 1355, so the sequence is purely periodic with period 1355. Under this model an exact finite computation over the whole period -- not merely over the stated domain -- shows the residue 1673 never occurs at all: it is not in the value set of the sequence. The domain [1,600] is therefore covered a fortiori. All arithmetic is exact integer arithmetic mod 2711; no floating point is used anywhere. To guard against the model being an artefact of a six-point fit on a sealed sequence, I bought ten held-out samples spread across the domain (n = 7, 40, 111, 157, 243, 337, 423, 463, 545, 600), deliberately including both endpoints and all five points where the model comes closest to 1673 (n = 545 -> 1677, 463 -> 1665, 243 -> 1682, 157 -> 1661, 423 -> 1687), since a near-miss is where a planted single-point deviation would be least detectable. All ten matched the model exactly (16/16 observations, 0 mismatches), and one evaluate call at the tightest near-miss n=545 returned holds=true, cross-checking that the proposition's own verdict agrees with the value channel. Residual risk, stated plainly: this is a blind sealed object, so the argument is a structural inference from 16 observed points, not an exhaustive check of 600. If the sealed sequence deviates from the fitted recurrence at one of the 584 unsampled points and lands exactly on 1673 there, my disposition is wrong. I judge that unlikely -- ten of ten held-out predictions, at 1/2711 chance each under any non-model hypothesis, is roughly 2^-114 of agreeing by accident -- but it is not zero, which is why confidence is not 1. Reproduction artifact: model_check.py; observation ledger: observations.json.
route_taken: I spent 6 calls recovering the generating law rather than scanning the domain, then 10 held-out samples plus 1 evaluate to falsify the recovered law -- 17 calls total -- because the scanning routes (range 1 600 at cost 600, or 600 evaluates) exceed the 120-credit budget outright and would have forced UNRESOLVED, while a correct closed form settles all 600 points at once and in fact settles the full period 1355.
what_would_resolve_it: Full certainty would need the remaining 584 points checked against the model, which costs 584 credits and is unaffordable here; alternatively, disclosure that the sealed generator is exactly an order-2 linear recurrence (i.e. that no point-defect was planted) would upgrade this to a proof, since 1673 is provably absent from the entire value set of 4*5^n + 3*6^n mod 2711.
